title: Hierarchical Conditional Tabular GAN for Multi-Tabular Synthetic Data Generation
summary: Proposes HCTGAN for relational databases, with a training algorithm that passes information from parent-table generators into the noise vector of child-table generators and a sampling algorithm that walks the schema so referential integrity holds by construction, and reports that it samples large volumes far faster than the probabilistic alternative at slightly lower quality. HCTGAN is presented as an extended version of CTGAN, keeping its generator loss and training-by-sampling and adding the parent conditioning on top; the comparison is against SDV's HMA1, on datasets shipped with the SDV Python library and scored with SDMetrics.
evidence: section 3 opens by presenting technical background on CTGAN before introducing the hierarchical elements, and states that HCTGAN is the authors' extended version of the CTGAN model; section 2 credits CTGAN with mode-specific normalisation, a conditional generator and training by sampling as improvements over TGAN; the generator definition says the model adheres to the generator loss and training-by-sampling process proposed by CTGAN but additionally conditions on a noise vector drawn from the parent tables, with the generators following a residual decoder architecture like CTGAN's; section 4.1 takes University_v1, Hepatitis_std_v1 and Pyrimidine_v1 from the SDV Python library and section 4.2 uses SDMetrics measures including KSComplement; Tables 1-3 report HCTGAN against HMA1 on each dataset, with the discussion noting HMA1 scores slightly better on quality but samples much more slowly and does not guarantee referential integrity

title: TabTreeFormer: Tabular Data Generation Using Hybrid Tree-Transformer
summary: Argues that transformers applied to tables lack the inductive biases that make tree ensembles effective on them, and answers with a hybrid in which a tree model supplies leaf-index prompts to the transformer while a dual-quantization tokenizer, K-means for modes and quantiles for precision, shortens sequences and shrinks the vocabulary, reaching competitive utility at a fraction of the model size. CTGAN is the acknowledged source of the multimodal-decomposition idea the tokenizer replaces and of the conditional generation the paper extends from single columns to clusters, but it is not among the eight generators run, where CTAB-GAN+ stands in for the GAN family.
evidence: section 1 states that the dual-quantization tokenization is inspired by Xu et al. (2019), which addresses multimodal continuous features via multimodal decomposition; section 2.1 records that CTGAN uses a variational Gaussian mixture model to decompose multimodal values; section 3 notes that many early tabular frameworks use conditional generation (Xu et al. 2019) based on the values of a specific column and that TabTreeFormer extends the condition to clusters with multiple concurrent conditions; the baselines in section 4 are Forest Diffusion, CTAB-GAN+, TTVAE, TabSyn, GReaT, REaLTabFormer, TabMT and TabuLa, with no CTGAN or TVAE row in the utility, fidelity, privacy or efficiency tables

title: Tabby: A Language Model Architecture for Tabular and Structured Data Synthesis
summary: Modifies a standard transformer language model for tabular synthesis by replacing selected layers with Gated Mixture-of-Experts blocks that give each column its own parameters, pairs this with a simpler row-serialisation training scheme, and reports quality at or near that of real data across eight tables and one nested JSON dataset. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN and VAE representatives among the non-language-model baselines, carried as rows through the machine-learning-efficacy, discrimination and distance-to-closest-record tables.
evidence: the Non-LLM Approaches paragraph in section 4 names CTGAN and TVAE, both cited to Xu et al. (2019), as the leading GAN and VAE approaches included alongside CTAB-GAN+ and four diffusion models; Table 2 reports CTGAN and TVAE machine-learning-efficacy scores across Diabetes, Travel, Adult, Magic, Shoppers, Abalone, Rainfall and House, and later tables report their discrimination and distance-to-closest-record scores on the same tables; section 5 notes that CTGAN and TVAE, unlike Tabby, do not clearly extend beyond tabular data to nested structures

title: A Closer Look on Memorization in Tabular Diffusion Model: A Data-Centric Perspective
summary: Traces memorization in tabular generative models back to individual training records, scoring each by how strongly and how early it is memorized over training epochs, and uses that score to drop the highest-contributing rows before training, combining the filter with a cut-and-mix augmentation into DynamicCutMix, which lowers memorization ratios without measurable cost to fidelity or downstream utility. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the three generators the method is trained on and measured against, and they carry the paper's transferability claim, since labels derived from the diffusion model are applied to them to show the memorization signal generalises across model families.
evidence: the abstract states that DynamicCut has transferability across generative models, with high-ranked samples identified from a diffusion model also effective when removed from GANs and VAEs; section 6.3 evaluates DynamicCutMix on three generative models, TabDDPM, CTGAN and TVAE, across Default, Shoppers and Adult, and Tables 2 and 3 report CTGAN and TVAE rows with their SMOTE, TCM, TCMP and DCM variants on memorization ratio, machine-learning efficacy, alpha-precision, beta-recall, shape, trend, C2ST and DCR; section 6.4 and Table 4 apply TabDDPM-derived memorization labels to CTGAN and TVAE, reporting a 23.75 per cent memorization reduction for CTGAN+DCM against 9.09 per cent for CTGAN+DCM-TabDDPM on Adult, which is the evidence for the cross-model claim; Figure 1 uses CTGAN, TVAE and TabDDPM as the overview models

title: StructSynth: Leveraging LLMs for Structure-Aware Tabular Data Synthesis in Low-Data Regimes
summary: Splits tabular synthesis into structure discovery and structure-guided generation: a directed acyclic graph is learned from the scarce real data, then supplied to a language model as an explicit blueprint of feature dependencies, so the generated rows respect the discovered structure rather than whatever correlations the model happens to infer, which improves fidelity and downstream utility over both implicit generators and unguided language models when data is thin. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the four deep generative baselines run across six datasets, and the paper's own citation trail attributes both the VAE line and the wider synthesis literature back to the Synthetic Data Vault paper.
evidence: the Baselines paragraph in section 4 lists TVAE (Xu et al. 2019), CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019), TabDDPM and NFlow as the deep generative model group among nine baselines; Table 2 reports CTGAN and TVAE downstream scores across Adult, Anxiety, Compas, Salary, Obesity and Churn with average ranks, and the privacy table reports their distinguishability scores on the same six; the discussion observes that CTGAN ranks highly on pairwise correlations but shows mediocre privacy and poor downstream utility; note that both the introduction and section 2 attribute VAEs and TVAE to Patki, Wedge and Veeramachaneni (2016), the Synthetic Data Vault paper, rather than to Xu et al., so the SDV paper carries part of the citation weight here

title: A Technical Exploration of Causal Inference with Hybrid LLM Synthetic Data
summary: Shows that synthetic tabular data can score well on train-on-synthetic-test-on-real prediction while badly misestimating the average treatment effect, and proposes a hybrid generator that synthesises covariates with a generative model but fits propensity and outcome models separately, so the treatment and outcome structure is preserved; it adds a pairing strategy for positivity violations and uses the unlimited synthetic sample to benchmark IPTW, AIPW and substitution estimators. A GAN-based generator supplies half the results and CTGAN is the only tabular GAN the paper cites or describes, credited with mode-specific normalisation and training-by-sampling, but the GAN rows are never tied to a named implementation.
evidence: section 2 (Related works) says CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) pioneered conditional GANs for tabular data, introducing mode-specific normalisation and training-by-sampling, and that GANs struggle with the conditional relationships causal inference needs; section 3 says generative encryption approaches are based on GANs, again citing Xu et al. (2019), and Xu et al. is the only tabular GAN reference in the bibliography; Tables 1 through 4 report GAN Syn Full, GAN Syn Hybrid and GAN Pair rows against LLM counterparts on TSTR AUC, IPTW and AIPW ATE estimates, bias, variance and MSE, so a GAN generator is run throughout, but no section names the implementation
needs: confirm which GAN implementation was run. CTGAN is the only tabular GAN cited or described, and the GAN rows carry half of Tables 1-4, but no section names the package; recorded unclear at confidence medium per the rule that unclear may not carry high confidence, with importance scoring how central the method is.
